prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1480; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a hit while turning left at an intersection. The insured reports the other vehicle struck the rear quarter as the claimant was completing a left turn. Claimant is not represented by counsel.

Entry 2: Verified that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant by phone. The account of the turn and the point of impact matched the first statement given at the scene, with no changes in sequence or detail.

Entry 4: Police report and two responding officers confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses were located to the collision itself.

Entry 5: Reviewed photos submitted by the claimant. They confirm the general location of the impact and the damaged panels. Damage pattern is largely consistent with the described angle of impact.

Entry 6: Checked prior claim history on the vehicle. No earlier damage to the same areas is on record, and no prior repairs were reported.

Entry 7: Claimant reports neck and shoulder pain beginning shortly after the collision, with a shoulder injury noted at the first medical visit. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type.

Entry 8: Medical records show the claimant had a small strain in the same shoulder area several years ago that healed fully. Treatment this time followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 9: Claim reviewed for next steps. Account has been consistent across all contacts, the damage and injury are in line with the impact described, and the file is ready for settlement evaluation.
